passage.text: Last week, Nam bought a pair of white shoes at a department store.
passage.reading: ˈlæst ˈwiːk, ˈnɑːm ˈbɔːt ə ˈpɛr əv ˈwaɪt ˈʃuːz ət ə dɪˈpɑːrtmənt ˌstɔːr.

passage.text: But after one day, she changed her mind: they were too tight.
passage.reading: bʌt ˈæftər ˈwʌn ˈdeɪ, ʃiː ˈtʃeɪndʒd hɜːr ˈmaɪnd: ðeɪ wɜːr ˈtuː ˈtaɪt.

passage.text: So on Saturday, she went back to the store with the shoes.
passage.reading: soʊ ɑːn ˈsætərdeɪ, ʃiː ˈwɛnt ˈbæk tə ðə ˈstɔːr wɪð ðə ˈʃuːz.

passage.text: "Can I get a refund, please?" she said to the woman at the store.
passage.reading: kən aɪ ˈɡɛt ə ˈriːfʌnd, ˈpliːz? ʃiː ˈsɛd tə ðə ˈwʊmən ət ðə ˈstɔːr.

passage.text: "I'm sorry, but our policy is no refunds after three days," the woman said.
passage.reading: aɪm ˈsɑːri, bʌt aʊr ˈpɑːləsi ɪz ˈnoʊ ˈriːfʌndz ˈæftər ˈθriː ˈdeɪz, ðə ˈwʊmən ˈsɛd.

passage.text: "But the shoes are in perfect condition, and I have the original box," Nam said.
passage.reading: bʌt ðə ˈʃuːz ər ɪn ˈpɜːrfɪkt kənˈdɪʃən, ənd aɪ ˈhæv ði əˈrɪdʒənəl ˈbɑːks, ˈnɑːm ˈsɛd.

passage.text: "I can give you store credit," the woman said.
passage.reading: aɪ kən ˈɡɪv juː ˈstɔːr ˈkrɛdɪt, ðə ˈwʊmən ˈsɛd.

passage.text: "You can use it in our store for a year."
passage.reading: juː kən ˈjuːz ɪt ɪn aʊr ˈstɔːr fər ə ˈjɪr.

passage.text: "OK. Can I use it for a new pair of shoes today?" she said.
passage.reading: oʊˈkeɪ. kən aɪ ˈjuːz ɪt fər ə ˈnuː ˈpɛr əv ˈʃuːz təˈdeɪ? ʃiː ˈsɛd.

passage.text: In the end, Nam left the store with a pair of black shoes in the right size.
passage.reading: ɪn ði ˈɛnd, ˈnɑːm ˈlɛft ðə ˈstɔːr wɪð ə ˈpɛr əv ˈblæk ˈʃuːz ɪn ðə ˈraɪt ˈsaɪz.
